items.title: Show HN: I gamified my daily GitHub commits with a growing garden
items.contentSnippet:
I often forgot to commit code, so I made Commitgarden. If you make at least one commit a day, your plant grows one stage. If you skip a day, it withers.
You log in with GitHub (read-only). It has a free plan to try it for a week. 
Please tell me what you think!

items.title: Show HN: Codex quota tracker Garmin watch face
items.contentSnippet:
I think I'm not alone with that quota-based AI subscriptions have given me a new hobby: checking how many tokens I have left.   How’s my 5-hour and 7-day limits? When’s the next reset? Can this task wait, or should I use a smaller model? I used to check my Garmin for steps and heart rate. Now I’ve built a watch face to track my AI usage limits and reset countdowns too. The idea was to make it very easy to add usage data from other vendors as well.

items.title: Show HN: You Can Just Filter YouTube Playlists in the 'Save to Playlist' Dialog
items.contentSnippet: Hi HN, I'm Cody, I have 847 YouTube playlists, and always hated that YouTube failed to provide basic playlist management tools. Ctrl+F was never convenient and breaks past 200 playlists. So I built & shipped my first Chrome extension. It replaces the Save dialog with a native-feeling searchable one that fetches all your playlists (and whether the current video is saved there) directly from YouTube's InnerTube API.
